newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 13.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on May 13. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The government has banned banners and pictures which suggest an alliance between the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri, the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

President Suharto has ordered Manpower Minister Abdul Latief to take action against the Indonesian Footwear Association for telling its members to delay paying minimum wages. The government increased the minimum wage in all 27 provinces by an average 10.07 percent from April 1. A worker in greater Jakarta now receives 172,500 rupiah ($75) monthly, compared with 156,000 rupiah in 1996.

Senior Bre-X Project Manager Jonathan Nassey has denied involvement in the Busang scandal. An independent audit found no economic gold deposit on the property while data pegged to the discovery had been falsified on an unprecedented scale.
